title: Binary Tree Postorder Traversal
prompt:
Given the `root` of a binary tree, return the values of its nodes in post-order traversal order (left subtree, then right subtree, then the node itself), using an iterative (non-recursive) approach.

The tree is given as a level-order array where `null` marks a missing child (the standard LeetCode serialization). Your function receives this array directly; the starter code includes a helper that builds the tree from it, so you only need to implement the traversal.

examples.explanation: Post-order visits the left subtree (empty for 1), right subtree (2's subtree: 3 then 2), then the root (1).

constraints: The number of nodes is in the range [0, 100]
hints: A neat trick: post-order (left, right, node) is the exact reverse of (node, right, left) — a traversal you can compute iteratively almost identically to pre-order.
Do a 'modified pre-order' with a stack, visiting node, then pushing left before right (so right is popped first), and prepend (or append then reverse at the end) each visited value.
If you append values to a list and reverse the whole list once at the end, you get the exact post-order sequence without any complex bookkeeping.

solution.approach: Post-order (left, right, node) is the mirror of (node, right, left). Compute the latter iteratively with a stack, exactly like pre-order but pushing left before right so right is processed first, and prepending each visited node's value to the front of the result (or equivalently appending and reversing once at the end). Reversing this 'node, right, left' sequence yields the true post-order.
